identification: Pair of 10x50 porro-prism binoculars in the 'Zeiss-type' (Z-type) layout: centre focus wheel at the top of a thin exposed focusing rod that runs down between the barrels to a separate lower bridge joining the objective ends, black pebbled covering, with a fitted brown leather case (saddle lid, side loops, strap). Most likely a 1950s-70s Japanese (or HK) commercial 10x50. On a second, closer look this is NOT the German WWII Dienstglas pattern Sonnet feared: Dienstglas 10x50s (thumbnails of the Zeiss BLC and 1939 Zeiss sales checked in Terapeak) have a thick full-length hinge and no exposed rod or separate lower bridge. The barrels only look tapered from the camera angle. Maker unread.

viewing_check: Read the top prism plates: maker (Nikon/Nippon Kogaku, Fujinon, Zeiss, Leitz, Hensoldt, Barr & Stroud, Ross), serial, '10x50', any military code (blc, cxn, beh, ddx, 'Dienstglas', broad arrow). Only a German WWII or a Nikon/Fujinon marking changes the verdict. Check prisms for fungus/haze and that the focus moves.
